old: It began as a small written page passed between two sides before a formal challenge.
In French and Italian it once meant a written note or card — only later did it come to mean secretive business teamwork.
A 19th-century German politician's use of 'Kartell' in parliament helped give this word its modern, corporate edge.
clues: This noun for a kind of alliance once named a formal note passed between rivals before a duel.

It means a group of independent companies that secretly agree to fix prices or limit supply, shadier than an ordinary partnership or merger. A German politician was the first to use it in the business sense.
Headlines speak of Mexican drug ones, and OPEC is often called an oil one. It shares an ancient root with 'card' and 'chart.'
reviewNote: Entry says first used, not coined.
